axioms.name: friedman_survey_data
axioms.note: literature premise (Friedman, EJC DS#7 2009): best-known packings and bounds for s(n), n <= 100; Goebel/Cottingham/Stenlund/Cantrell pattern families

axioms.name: nagamochi_theorem
axioms.note: theorem premise (Nagamochi 2005): s(k^2-2) = s(k^2-1) = k for all k - grid optimal for these n, no improvement possible

axioms.name: kearney_shiu_s6
axioms.note: theorem premise (Kearney-Shiu 2002): s(6) = 3 - our engine's REFUSAL to pack 6 squares below 3 is consistent with this theorem

axioms.name: competition_metric
axioms.note: rules premise: score = sum(L/sqrt(n) - 1); missing puzzle charged the grid ceiling; partial submissions allowed

axioms.name: engine_instrument
axioms.note: instrument premise: the pressure-settling engine is a MEASURED search instrument (float64, deterministic LCG); certification margin 1e-9 declared

axioms.name: optimality_open
axioms.note: conversational premise: for most n the optimal s(n) is unknown; found packings are upper bounds only

lemmas.name: cascade_count_symbolic
lemmas.gap: requires omega/ring (Mathlib) or manual algebra; the closure count is verified concretely at every cascade step in scripts/column3/05 (two-path: recursive vs. closed form)

lemmas.name: verification_margin_soundness
lemmas.gap: stand-in for the soundness certificate: proving that float64 SAT separation with a 1e-9 margin implies true non-overlap requires interval-arithmetic formalization (Mathlib) or exact algebraic predicates (exact predicates on rotated squares); our certificate is MEASURED with declared margin, not machine-checked

lemmas.name: s11_optimal_value
lemmas.gap: DELIBERATE TARGET, EXPECTED UNPROVEN: no closed characterization of s(11) (or any non-trivial s(n)) is known; optimality proofs exist only for n in {1..8, 10, 14, 15, 24, 35} and square/adjacent families. This sorry marks the combinatorial-geometry wall of the competition
